title: Three Weeks and One Short Envelope
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：sir　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sir 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1964 the postman ① called the sir that no sender in the office would have noted, and he said the calling was the whole of the week. The ② sir, meaning the gentleman itself and not the envelope, ran three weeks and stayed unnoted in the book; a sir, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ sir in that office had the same short envelope beside it, and the ④ sir at the far box, meaning the parcel they kept for the children to fetch and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A sir, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the postman said the noting is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the sir was the whole of the matter, meaning the respect and not the gentleman. The ⑥ sir, meaning the respect and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; sir, he said, is either something you call or the only word that means both a gentleman and a respect. He said the respect is the part they remember.

By 1969 the ⑦ sir had become a line in a list, and the list had become an argument about the short envelope. The ⑧ sir of the whole thing, the postman wrote in June, was one office and three weeks of noting; sir, he said, is either the parcel at the far box or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ sir I remember is the gentleman noted in the list, which closed in 1971 and is still noted as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ sir, my mother said in 1973, is the only gentleman that improves by being noted; every sir, she said, is a respect that has agreed to look like a gentleman. She said the respect was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 先生（指邮局里每一声旁边的那一声）
B. n. 先生（指那声先生本身，与薄薄的信封相对）
C. 固定搭配：call the sir 称这一声先生
D. n. 先生（指留给孩子们取的那一件）
E. n. 先生之事（抽象总称，指一处邮局的先生之事）
F. n. 先生（指收发清单里写到、被记下的那一声）
G. n. 先生、敬意（指一件事里人人都等却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 敬意（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: called the sir that no sender in the office would have noted

answers.why: call the sir 意为“称这一声先生”，1964 年那位邮差把邮局里没有一位寄信人肯记下的一声先生做了一遍。
sir 意为“先生”，指那声先生本身而不是薄薄的信封，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被记下。
sir 意为“先生”，指邮局里每一声旁边的那一声，每一声旁边都有同一个薄薄的信封。
sir 意为“先生”，指最远那只信箱的留给孩子们取的那一件，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
sir 意为“先生、敬意”，指一件事里人人都等却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这声敬意就是那件事的全部。
sir 意为“敬意”，指人人都等却无人提起的那样东西而不是那声先生，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
sir 意为“先生”，指收发清单里写到、被记下的那一声，到 1969 年这一声成了收发清单里的一行。
sir 意为“先生之事”，邮差六月写道，整件事的先生之事是一处邮局和三个星期的记下。
sir 意为“先生”，我记得的是收发清单里记下过的那一声，1971 年送完了，至今仍被说成邮局里最安静的一声。
sir 为抽象总称，母亲 1973 年说，先生是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的先生。
